item.title: Ep. 160 - So, You Want To Own A Business [Business 300]
item.description: If you want to own and operate a business, don’t start with finding your passion. Figure out what others are struggling with and how you can help them. Solve other people’s problems. Start by focusing on potential customers, then continue your focus on existing customers, and then focus on future customers. Customers, not passions, are what make a business.If you want to be in business, focus on others first. Start by giving, not taking. And many a time, when you focus on serving others, your find your passions.
item.author: Philip Kulishov

item.title: Ep. 159 - Systems Bring Residual Return [Business 300]
item.description:
These are larger projects that have a lot of steps and milestones before the result can be actualized. But the return on them is big. These are your annual or quarterly goals that you have to work on for weeks or month to make progress on. In order to get where you want to get to, you need to devote most of your time on these items, and make sure you're keeping yourself on task. The payoff is big. But it won't happen right away.

Systems bring residual return.

item.title: Ep. 158 - Action Over Vision [Business 300]
item.description:
Business owners are visionaries. They're dreamers. They're goal setters. They focus on the future, with aspirations then and there. 

Vague notions of ambition and aspiration that sound like, "It'd be great if..." aren't strong enough to get you anywhere, and definitely not strong enough to lead others with. Any leader must have clarity in his vision for the future and must be able to communicate it clearly.

Get clear on your actions. Thats where the results come from. You need to prioritize action over vision.
item.author: Philip Kulishov
item.itunes:author: Philip Kulishov

item.title: Ep. 157 - How To Move Fast [Business 300]
item.description:
The typical amount of things that the average person gets done on a week by week basis isn't very much. There usually isn't too much actual progress made by most people.

But in business, you have a natural motivator to keep you going; a personal incentive to whip you into action. Profit.

Business requires that we move fast. But won't going too fast hurt you? If you can't keep up with the pace, won't that in itself be your downfall?


It could be. So, how then should we approach the speed of execution?
